citing_sentence: Notably, the saliency of weights is determined by analyzing the activation space (sensitivities) of the base model rather than just regularizing based on the weight space, similar to [10,26].
cited_title: Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
primary_explanation: OGD is described as a parameter-space/gradient-projection method that restricts gradient directions to avoid interference with previous tasks; it does not present an approach that determines weight saliency via activation-space sensitivity analysis. Citing OGD as similar to an activation-space saliency method is therefore misleading.
secondopinion_reasoning: The cited paper does not discuss determining the saliency of weights by analyzing the activation space. Instead, it focuses on Orthogonal Gradient Descent (OGD), which involves projecting gradients to avoid interference with previous tasks. The paper emphasizes preserving knowledge by maintaining orthogonal gradient directions, not by analyzing activation spaces or sensitivities as claimed in the citing sentence.
